root_cause.text: xfrm_migrate_policy_find() in the xfrm policy subsystem incorrectly took an extra reference on the returned xfrm_policy by calling xfrm_pol_hold_rcu() after xfrm_policy_lookup_bytype() had already returned the policy with a held reference, causing a refcount imbalance and leak.
root_cause.evidence: The patch deletes the xfrm_pol_hold_rcu(pol) block from xfrm_migrate_policy_find(), and both the CVE and commit message explicitly state that “the lookup function already returns a policy with held reference, making the second call redundant,” which caused the memory leak in xfrm_policy_alloc.

agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch deletes the xfrm_pol_hold_rcu(pol) block from xfrm_migrate_policy_find(), and both the CVE and commit message explicitly state that “the lookup function already returns a policy with held reference, making the second call redundant,” which caused the memory leak in xfrm_policy_alloc.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix xfrm_migrate_policy_find() to return a successfully looked-up policy without failing it on an unnecessary xfrm_pol_hold_rcu() check.
intent_record.what: The change removes a three-line conditional block after xfrm_policy_lookup_bytype() that called xfrm_pol_hold_rcu(pol) and set pol = NULL when that call returned false, leaving the function to return the looked-up policy directly after the existing IS_ERR_OR_NULL(pol) check and RCU unlock.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function no longer attempts to acquire an additional RCU-based hold on the returned xfrm_policy and no longer converts a successfully looked-up policy into NULL when that hold acquisition fails. This allows the found policy to be returned as-is, avoiding dropped lookup results caused by the extra hold check.

grouping_result.intent: Fix xfrm_migrate_policy_find() to return a successfully looked-up policy without failing it on an unnecessary xfrm_pol_hold_rcu() check.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly fixes xfrm_migrate_policy_find() by removing the unnecessary xfrm_pol_hold_rcu() handling after xfrm_policy_lookup_bytype() already returns a referenced policy, which matches the described refcount imbalance/root cause.

candidates.rationale: This is the direct root cause: it takes an additional reference on a policy already returned with a held reference by xfrm_policy_lookup_bytype(), creating the refcount imbalance and leak.

candidates.content: pol = xfrm_policy_lookup_bytype(net, type, &fl, sel->family, dir, if_id);
candidates.rationale: This lookup already returns the policy with a held reference; its interaction with the subsequent extra xfrm_pol_hold_rcu() explains why the later hold is erroneous.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement is the vulnerable operation: it takes an additional reference on `pol` even though `xfrm_policy_lookup_bytype()` already returned the policy with a held reference, causing a refcount imbalance and resulting leak.

bic_trace_step.reason: The shown function body is sufficient because it includes the relevant reference-handling logic in xfrm_migrate_policy_find(). The root cause is an extra reference taken after xfrm_policy_lookup_bytype() already returned a policy with a held reference. In this commit version, the function still does exactly that: after obtaining `pol`, it checks `if (IS_ERR_OR_NULL(pol)) goto out_unlock;` and then executes `if (!xfrm_pol_hold_rcu(pol)) pol = NULL;`. That `xfrm_pol_hold_rcu(pol)` is the vulnerable construct described in the root cause: it takes an additional reference on the returned policy. This commit only fixes a null-dereference bug by changing `xfrm_pol_hold_rcu(ret)` to `xfrm_pol_hold_rcu(pol)` and removing `ret`; it does not remove the unnecessary hold. Therefore the vulnerable extra refcount increment is still present, so `has_bug=true` and `is_fixed=false`.
